title: Introduction to HTML
subtitle: Learn how the web begins
description: Understand what HTML is, how web pages are structured, and how to create your first HTML document.

blocks.text: Introduction to HTML
Welcome to your first HTML lesson. HTML is the language used to structure content on the web.
When you visit a website, the browser receives HTML and uses it to understand what the page contains.
HTML can describe headings, paragraphs, links, images, buttons, forms, tables, and many other parts of a webpage.
HTML does not normally control the visual appearance of a website by itself. CSS is mainly responsible for styling, while JavaScript is commonly used to add behavior and interaction.
The word HTML stands for HyperText Markup Language.

blocks.question: What does HTML stand for?
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct! HTML stands for HyperText Markup Language.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Not quite. HTML means HyperText Markup Language.
blocks.reasoning: HTML describes the structure of content using markup. The browser reads that markup and builds the webpage structure from it.

blocks.text: Your First HTML Document
A basic HTML document contains several important parts. The document type declaration tells the browser that the page uses modern HTML.
The html element contains the complete HTML document.
The head element contains information about the document that is generally not displayed as the main page content.
The body element contains the content that users normally see on the webpage.

blocks.title: A basic HTML document
blocks.code:
Hello, Code Academy!

This is my first webpage.
blocks.output:
Hello, Code Academy!
This is my first webpage.

blocks.text: The first line, DOCTYPE html, tells the browser that this document uses HTML5.
The h1 element creates a main heading, while the p element creates a paragraph.

blocks.question: Which HTML element is normally used for the largest main heading?
blocks.correctFeedback: Excellent! The h1 element is normally used for the main heading.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: The correct answer is <h1>. It represents the highest-level heading.
blocks.reasoning: HTML provides heading levels from h1 through h6. The h1 element represents the highest-level heading in the document structure.

blocks.text: Understanding HTML Elements
HTML documents are built from elements. Many elements have an opening tag, content, and a closing tag.
For example, a paragraph can be written using an opening p tag and a closing p tag.
The text between the opening and closing tags is the content of the element.
Some HTML elements do not need a separate closing tag. These are commonly called void elements.

blocks.question: Which element is used to create a paragraph?
blocks.correctFeedback:
Correct! The

element represents a paragraph.
blocks.reasoning: The p element is the standard HTML element for representing a paragraph of text.

blocks.text: HTML Attributes
HTML elements can also have attributes. Attributes provide additional information about an element.
Attributes are normally written inside the opening tag and usually have a name and a value.
In this example, href is the attribute and its value tells the browser where the link should lead.

blocks.question: What does the href attribute commonly specify on an anchor element?
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct! href specifies the destination of a link.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: The correct answer is the destination of the link.
blocks.reasoning: The href attribute provides the URL or destination that the browser should navigate to when the link is activated.

blocks.text: Practice
Now you have seen the basic structure of an HTML document, HTML elements, and HTML attributes.
The best way to become comfortable with HTML is to write the code yourself and observe what the browser produces.

blocks.title: Your first practice page
blocks.code:
My Name

I am learning HTML at Code Academy.

Visit a website

blocks.question: Which part of an HTML document normally contains the content displayed on the webpage?
blocks.correctFeedback: Excellent! The body contains the main content displayed on the webpage.
blocks.reasoning: The body element contains the document's main visible content, such as headings, paragraphs, images, links, buttons, and other webpage elements.

blocks.text: Lesson Complete
You have completed your introduction to HTML.
You now understand what HTML is, how a basic HTML document is structured, what elements are, and how attributes provide additional information.
In the next lesson, you will continue building your HTML knowledge with more elements and practical examples.
